title: Grateful Dead Live at Family Dog at the Great Highway on 1969-11-02
venue: Family Dog at the Great Highway
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> SEK'D Prodif Plus -> Samplitude v8.01 Professional -> FLAC
source: Disc 1: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat (44.1k) DDisc 2: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat (44.1k) D

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture with excellent clarity (aside from brief digital glitches) of a psychedelic‑heavy 11/2/69 show highlighted by an epic Dark Star and stellar Death Don't Have No Mercy.
ai_review.review: The Charlie Miller soundboard transfer delivers a generally crisp, deep mix that lets the band’s 48‑minute Dark Star shine, though listeners should expect short digital noise bursts around the 5:30‑6:00 mark. Musically the concert is a high‑water mark of late‑1969 Dead, featuring a monster Dark Star, soaring Good Lovin', a powerful Death Don't Have No Mercy and memorable moments like Jerry’s scream at the end of The Eleven. Pigpen’s three‑song run, Tom Constanten’s keyboards and Mickey Hart’s added percussion round out an exhilarating set.

ai_rating.rationale: The overwhelming majority of reviews are five stars praising the performance and mix; a few note minor digital glitches, pulling the average slightly below perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear, deep sound with excellent balance; brief digital distortion/noise in Dark Star (5:16‑5:23, 5:30‑5:37, 5:55‑6:07) noted by several reviewers.

standout_songs: St. Stephen > The Eleven > Death Don't Have No Mercy
show_quality.setlist_flow: The early psychedelic segment (Cold Rain, Dark Star) is praised as electrifying, while the later folk‑rock portion receives mixed comments but still contains strong performances such as Death Don't Have No Mercy.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His guitar tone on Dark Star and the iconic scream at the end of The Eleven are highlighted as standout moments.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is described as deep, clear, and "beyond amazing" throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Bob: Praised for his country‑flavored rendition of Seasons of My Heart and overall solid rhythm work.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s keyboards add richness and expand the sonic palette, freeing Pigpen to focus on percussion.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey Hart’s addition provides a new layer of rhythmic depth that enhances the later set.
